clue.text: Education officials in formal meeting becoming incandescent

indicators.note: in places the officials inside the meeting, splitting its letters

parts.note: an AGM is an annual general meeting, a formal gathering of members
LEA is a Local Education Authority, the British body that runs schools in an area

explanation.surface: School administrators at a stiff annual meeting get heated and start glowing with rage.
explanation.walkthrough: A Local Education Authority is the British council body that runs state schools in an area. 'incandescent' suggests fury in the surface but here means glowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something shining or glowing with light, as when hot metal gleams.

clue.text: Work out manoeuvring to break into radio as dogsbody

indicators.note: to break into says the following letters are pushed inside the radio band

parts.note: FM, frequency modulation, is a radio band
to act is to work or function

indicators.note: manoeuvring means the letters of out are moved about

explanation.surface: Someone trying to work out how to get into broadcasting starts as a lowly assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work out' reads as one phrase meaning solve, but splits into a verb for function and the anagram fodder for 'manoeuvring'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogsbody is a servant or assistant who does all sorts of menial jobs; the Latin-derived word means a do-everything helper.

clue.text: Amazed finding doctors involved in some French business

indicators.note: involved in says the doctors are wrapped up inside the following letters

parts.note: du is French for 'some' (partitive article)
truck means dealings or business, as in 'have no truck with'
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, so MBS are doctors

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished to find medics mixed up in some shady French affair.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUCK in the sense of dealings survives mainly in 'have no truck with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being struck speechless with astonishment is being utterly astonished.

clue.text: Left out of exotic place, Peru's capital

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange and transformed, so the letters are rearranged
out of says the letter for left is removed from place

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone, having left an exotic spot, heads for Lima, Peru's capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes L from PLACE to leave PACE; 'exotic' rearranges PACE PERUS. 'capital' looks like Lima but means a capital letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital letters are the large letters of the alphabet, as opposed to small or lower-case ones.

clue.text: Cracked engine

definitions.meaning: cracked here means crazy, mad (a slang sense)
short for locomotive, the railway engine

explanation.surface: A railway engine with a crack in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang Spanish-derived word for mad, and also a clipped form of the word for a railway engine.

clue.text: 17 misheard Sky broadcast

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 17-across, phrase for a dying utterance

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A dying speech is misheard on a Sky TV broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Nelson's dying words to Captain Hardy at Trafalgar; legend says he really said 'Kismet' (fate), so 'misheard' fits the story as well as being fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the reputed dying words of Admiral Nelson, the most famous example of a deathbed utterance.

clue.text: Goes aimlessly around Sweden, stumped!

indicators.note: around says the potters-about word encloses the letter for Sweden

parts.note: to footle is to mess about or potter aimlessly, so footles means goes aimlessly
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: Someone wanders round Sweden aimlessly and is completely baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stumped!' is taken literally: someone reduced to stumps has no feet, hence the exclamation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A person without feet stands on stumps, so lacking feet is humorously being stumped.

clue.text: Burial site round ancient city means to make an impression

indicators.note: round says the burial site goes around the ancient city

parts.note: a grave is where someone is buried
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A tomb around an old city is a way of leaving a mark on history.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an engraving-based printing process, a method of pressing an image onto paper.

clue.text: Items of dance music they won't take off

indicators.note: items of says the answer is a portion found within the phrase dance music

explanation.surface: Some dance tracks never get going.
explanation.definitionFit: These large Australian birds are flightless, so they can never leave the ground.

clue.text: Condition of volume penned by Nick mostly

indicators.note: penned by says the pieces are shut inside, as in a pen
mostly means the last letter is dropped from the word for nick

parts.note: nick is British slang for prison
o' is the shortened form of of, as in man o' war

explanation.surface: A book's printing terms were drawn up in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims PRISON to PRISO; O and V go inside. 'Nick' is British slang for a prison or police station.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipulation or clause attached to an agreement is a condition.

clue.text: Reactionary state cut down monster, 17

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 17-across, phrase for a dying utterance

indicators.note: reactionary means going backwards, so the trimmed word is read in reverse
cut down means the last letter is removed from the word for state

parts.note: to utter is to state or say
a brute is a beast or monster

explanation.surface: A right-wing government cut a monster down to size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' trims UTTER to UTTE, and 'Reactionary' reverses it to ETTU.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar's reputed dying words to his assassin, as Shakespeare has them, are a celebrated deathbed line.

clue.text: Start where film is made

explanation.surface: The point where a movie begins shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: The beginning of something, and also a two-word phrase for being at the filming location.

clue.text: Whit, time for this composition?

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount, as is a mote or speck

explanation.surface: Whitsun is the time for this church piece?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whit' suggests Whitsun, a church festival, which suits a sacred piece; here it means a speck.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a short polyphonic choral piece, usually sacred, so a musical composition.

clue.text: Summon archdeacon to tuck into ice-cream

indicators.note: to tuck into says the clergyman goes inside, as well as suggesting eating

parts.note: a cone is an ice-cream cornet
Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: Someone calls a senior cleric over to enjoy an ice-cream.
explanation.walkthrough: An archdeacon is styled 'the Venerable', abbreviated Ven.
explanation.definitionFit: To call people together or assemble a meeting is to summon them.

clue.text: Stormy Red Sea — Wren gets anchor maybe

indicators.note: stormy suggests turbulence, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A Wren, a Royal Navy servicewoman, in a rough Red Sea gets hold of the ship's anchor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anchor' is not the ship's but the presenter who anchors a news programme. A Wren was a member of the Women's Royal Naval Service.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor is the main presenter of a television news bulletin, an example of a broadcaster reading news.

clue.text: Host's pelf dissipated in dens of iniquity

indicators.note: dissipated means scattered, so the letters are dispersed into a new order

explanation.surface: A host's ill-gotten money is squandered in places of vice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dissipated' doubles as a hint at a debauched life, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Places offering luxurious, immoral pleasures such as brothels are seedy dens of vice.

clue.text: Star's awful moods could produce ironic comment

indicators.note: could produce says the letters of the preceding words can be made into something new

explanation.surface: A celebrity's terrible temper might lead to a sarcastic remark.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used ironically of a confident statement that is soon proved wrong.

clue.text: Fine work of art, very attractive

parts.note: F is the pencil abbreviation for fine
an etching is a print made from an etched plate

explanation.surface: A fine piece of art is extremely appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Charming and good-looking describe someone appealing, the same sense as attractive.

clue.text: Love to be embraced by career girl that's attractive and rather plump

indicators.note: to be embraced by says love is held inside the word for career

parts.note: to career is to run headlong
love is nil in tennis, the letter O
a dish is slang for an attractive person

explanation.surface: A career woman who is attractive gets a hug and turns out a little chubby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' is the verb, to rush along, not a profession.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -ish means somewhat, so somewhat round in shape is a tactful word for slightly plump.

clue.text: Russian transport tsar arranged to carry common type

indicators.note: to carry says the rearranged ruler's letters hold the lout inside
arranged means the letters of tsar are put in a new order

parts.note: oik is British slang for a common, uncouth person

explanation.surface: The tsar's carriage was arranged to take along an ordinary passenger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' makes TRAS from TSAR; 'to carry' puts OIK in it. OIK is British slang for a lout.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian vehicle drawn by three horses abreast is a traditional form of transport there.

clue.text: Monster so upset Nazi troops

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, so
the SS was the elite Nazi paramilitary corps

explanation.surface: A monster so upset the Nazi soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so' looks like a link but stands for ERGO, which 'upset' turns over.
explanation.definitionFit: A female ogre, a giant man-eating creature of folklore, is a kind of monster.

clue.text: Birds finally in flight move energetically

indicators.note: in says the final letter goes inside the word for flight

parts.note: a rout is a disorderly retreat or flight

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of birds

explanation.surface: Birds take to the air at last and fly vigorously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' looks avian but means a fleeing army.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir someone out or rouse them into action is to make them move briskly.

clue.text: Personnel detained by criminal organisation, the mob

indicators.note: detained by says the staff letters are held inside the gang

parts.note: a tong is a Chinese secret society, often criminal
HR, human resources, is the personnel department

explanation.surface: Staff are held captive by a gang, the Mafia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the mob' looks like the Mafia but means a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A large dense crowd of people is a mob in the sense of a teeming multitude.

clue.text: Blame having lost university safe investment

indicators.note: having lost means a letter is taken away from the word for blame

parts.note: guilt is culpability, blame

explanation.surface: A graduate with no university place is blamed for poor investments.
explanation.walkthrough: GILTS are British government bonds, treated as very low-risk investments.
explanation.definitionFit: A gilt-edged security, a UK government bond, is a low-risk holding.

clue.text: See 6
Frenchman certainly very engaging

indicators.note: engaging means holding within, so the agreement word takes in the letter

parts.note: yes is a way of saying certainly

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is certainly very charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaging' looks like charming but means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A common French given name for a man, as in the designer Saint Laurent.

clue.text: Couple at Buckingham Palace are flirting

parts.note: the royal residence's famous couple supplies the Duke of Edinburgh, Prince Philip, shortened to Phil
a couple is a pair joined together, written out with the joining word between them
the second of the palace couple is the late Queen, whose cipher is ER (Elizabeth Regina)

explanation.surface: The royal pair at the palace are flirting.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue words name both royals at once, Prince Philip and ER (Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's cipher), so the pair is written out as a 4,3,2 phrase joined by 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: To dally or womanise casually is to engage in flirtatious affairs; they do it as they are flirting.

clue.text: New climb under development

parts.note: an ascent is a climb

explanation.surface: A new climbing route is still being developed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something just coming into being and starting to grow is still emerging and developing.

clue.text: Insurgent's ultimate cause — this?

indicators.note: ultimate picks the final letter of the word insurgent

parts.note: a reason is a cause or motive

explanation.surface: Is betrayal of the state what a rebel finally fights for?
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimate' takes T, the last letter of 'Insurgent' (the 's is ignored); the whole clue then describes what a rebel is guilty of.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country by rebelling against it is the crime an insurgent commits.
